items.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: I remember hearing the drummer Louis Hayes once in a club

ctx.x: Yeah. Generally everybody feels the time kind of where they feel it, and they can coexist. I mean Elvin played so fucking behind and so wide. And even in Harry’s band, Arthur Latin, great drummer. We’ve been playing together for years and years. He kind of plays behind and I kind of play on top a little bit — or in the middle or on top and it works. You know it can work. Yeah.
I remember hearing the drummer Louis Hayes once in a club and he was so on top of the beat I said how does this music not just keep speeding up until it’s impossible. And it didn’t. But he was like —

Right. Because you can be on top of the beat and not rush. It’s about anticipation. Yeah. I don’t know, that’s an interesting kind of an existential thing, time you know. The concept of time. But I know for me, like I say, I kind of play on top or play in the middle. And generally if I’m with a drummer who plays on top of me it can be uncomfortable. Because sometimes it’s better to have the counteract a little bit. I mean it’s better to just have it if you were playing right in the middle. But everybody feels it…
